title: Logo in the bottom-right corner
description: The fixture logo (wmu: xi://local/watermark/logo.png, visible in the URL) 16 px from the south-east corner, at 80% opacity and scaled to 20% of the image.

title: Top-left with offsets
description: The fixture logo (wmu) at gravity nowe with 24 px offsets from the top-left corner; x and y always point inwards from the gravity's edges.

title: Large faded mark in the centre
description: The fixture logo (wmu) centred (ce), half the image wide and 30% opaque: the classic proof watermark.

title: Bottom edge, centred
description: The fixture logo (wmu) at gravity so (south) with a 20 px offset up from the bottom edge.

title: Every corner (chained pipelines)
description: Each chained pipeline draws its own watermark (each with its own wmu): nowe, noea, sowe and soea, 12 px from the edges.

title: Fixed-size box (wms)
description: watermark_size fits the fixture logo (wmu) into 160 px wide (height from its aspect ratio) instead of a fraction of the image; it applies when the wm scale is 0.

title: Drop shadow (wmsh)
description: watermark_shadow draws the fixture logo's (wmu) alpha in black, blurred with sigma 4, under it: the logo stays readable on light areas.

title: Rotated (wmr)
description: watermark_rotate turns the fixture logo (wmu) 20° clockwise onto a transparent bounding box before it is placed.

title: Tiled over the image (re)
description: Position re (replicate) repeats the fixture logo (wmu) over the whole image; the x and y offsets are the spacing between tiles.

title: Rotated tiles
description: Replicated tiles of the fixture logo (wmu) turned 30° counter-clockwise (wmr:-30): a diagonal pattern that is hard to crop out.

title: Chessboard (ch)
description: Position ch tiles a 2×2 unit (tile, empty, empty, tile) of the fixture logo (wmu) centred on a tile: half the density of re; the offsets are the spacing.

title: Per-request image (wmu)
description: watermark_url picks the watermark per request: a fixture of the local source, resolved against the source allowlist like any source. The playground base64-encodes it.

title: SVG watermark from a URL
description: A public SVG (sanitised on the server) as the per-request watermark, bottom-left on the parrots.

title: Text: semi-transparent “© 2026 Studio” footer
description: watermark_text takes Pango markup (font, size, colour, alpha, weight); a soft shadow keeps it readable. The playground base64-encodes the markup.

title: Text: two lines, two fonts
description: Markup with a newline: a bold yellow title over a smaller monospace line (the image ships DejaVu Sans and DejaVu Sans Mono).
pipelines: Golden hour Paris · 2026

title: Text: repeated “DRAFT” stamp
description: A 35% alpha word, rotated 30° and tiled with 60 px spacing.

title: Watermark on an animated GIF
description: The fixture logo (wmu) is drawn once over the joined frames, so every frame of the animation carries it.

title: Resize, then watermark, as WebP
description: Pipeline 1 smart-crops to 600×400; pipeline 2 runs on that result, so the text sits in the corner of the final image; the output is WebP at quality 80.

title: Default watermark (imgproxy compatibility)
description: wm without wmu or wmt draws the server's default watermark image, XI_PROCESSING_WATERMARK_SOURCE (the equivalent of imgproxy's IMGPROXY_WATERMARK_PATH/URL; empty by default). The image is not in the URL, so every other example names its watermark explicitly; this one works only on a deployment that configures it.

title: imgix: txt footer
description: imgix's txt family: plain text (escaped for Pango) with font, size, ARGB colour, alignment, padding and shadow.

title: imgix: mark in the top-right corner
description: mark takes an image URL (here a fixture of the local source); mark-align, mark-pad, mark-alpha and mark-scale place it.

title: imgix: tiled and rotated mark
description: mark-tile=grid repeats the mark; mark-rot turns it (counter-clockwise, as in imgix).

title: Cloudinary: l_text with fl_layer_apply
description: A text layer (family_size_style:text) coloured and faded in its own component, placed by the fl_layer_apply component that closes the group. Each chained pipeline is one component.

title: Cloudinary: l_fetch image layer
description: l_fetch:<base64url> overlays a remote image (a public SVG); w_0.15 with fl_relative sizes it to 15% of the base image.

title: Cloudinary: fl_tiled
description: The same layer rotated (a_20), faded (o_30) and tiled over the image with fl_tiled.

title: ImageKit: l-image overlay
description: An image layer from the mount's source (@@ stands for /): 80 px wide, 80% opaque, 16 px from the bottom-right corner (lx-N, ly-N count from the far edges), after a resize in the same step.

title: ImageKit: l-text overlay
description: A text layer: font size, colour, bold (tg-b) and alpha (al, 1-9), 16 px from the bottom-left corner, in a chained step after the resize.

title: imaginary: /watermark (text)
description: imaginary's text endpoint on the query mount, written by hand (raw mode): text, font, colour, opacity, wrap width and tile margin; tiled like imaginary (noreplicate=true draws one).

title: imaginary: /watermarkimage
description: imaginary's image watermark: the image URL placed at left/top with an opacity.

title: Trim and resize to WebM
description: /video cuts 1.2 s from 0.4 s (exact: from the keyframe before it), scales the 1280×720 clip down to 480 px wide and writes VP9 + Opus WebM. Drag the trim handles on the timeline to change the cut.

title: HLS stream with a two-rung ladder
description: The @m3u8 extension (or stream:hls) answers an HLS master playlist instead of a file: 360p and 240p renditions of the 6.6 s clip in 2 s CMAF segments, each transcoded when a player asks for it, the audio encoded once. Safari plays it here; other browsers list its playlists, served through the playground's api/stream.

title: HLS with MPEG-TS segments (older players)
description: segment_format:ts writes the stream for players older than HLS 7 (smart TVs, set-top boxes): version 3 playlists whose .ts segments carry H.264 and the AAC audio together, each muxed on its own with the stream's timestamps. H.264 only, so gpl images only. The MP4 source's audio is encoded in chunks of whole segments.

title: HLS with a logo and a timecode on every rendition
description: Watermarks work on streams: the logo (wmu) from 1 s to 5 s and a running timecode on each segment of each rendition, timed on the stream (across the 2 s segment boundaries), laid out on the 360p rendition and scaled to the 240p one so it does not move when the player switches.

title: Audio file → MP3 with loudness normalisation
description: An audio-only output: the stereo tones, normalised to -16 LUFS / -1.5 dBTP / 11 LU (EBU R128, single-pass loudnorm) and encoded with LAME at 128 kbit/s.

title: Logo on a clip, faded in and out
description: The image watermark options (wm, wmu) as a video overlay: the fixture logo in the bottom-right corner, shown from 0.4 s to 1.8 s (overlay_window) with 0.3 s fades (overlay_fade).

title: Running timecode overlay
description: timecode draws the output's running time (HH:MM:SS.mmm) with FFmpeg drawtext in the top-left corner, 28 px; no request text reaches FFmpeg.

title: Waveform picture of an audio file
description: waveform renders the audio as an 800×200 PNG (FFmpeg showwavespic, encoded by libvips): one blue band per channel on white, like Cloudinary's fl_waveform.

title: /q/video: a muted 320 px WebM
description: The query form of /video: every option is a query key (start, duration, width, mute, format), signed with xi_sig over /video + the query.

title: Cloudinary: /video/upload trim
description: Cloudinary's video URL on the demo's local source: so_ and du_ cut 1.2 s from 0.4 s, w_480 with c_limit scales it down, f_webm writes WebM.

title: Video preset: a 2 s muted preview
description: preset:preview expands the demo's video preset (XI_VIDEO_TRANSFORM_PRESETS: duration:2/resize:fit:320:0/mute:1/format:webm) in place; start:0.4 after it moves the cut. With XI_VIDEO_TRANSFORM_UNSIGNED_POLICY=restricted, unsigned URLs may hold presets only (plus the allowed options).

title: Cloudinary: t_ named transformation on a video
description: t_web names the demo's video preset (854 px wide, quality 60, WebM); so_ and du_ cut 1.2 s from 0.4 s on top of it. The preset's format wins over the public ID's .mp4 extension, as a named transformation's f_ does.

title: Cloudflare: /cdn-cgi/media mode=audio
description: Cloudflare Media Transformations' audio mode: the clip's sound track (duration=1s, Cloudflare's shortest cut) as M4A (AAC).

title: Cloudflare: /cdn-cgi/media mode=spritesheet
description: Cloudflare's sprite sheet mode on the image path: four 160×90 frames spread over the first second, in a JPEG grid.

title: ImageKit: video resize to WebM
description: ImageKit's video transformations on a video file key: w-320 and h-180 (maintain_ratio, a cover crop), f-webm.

title: Trim: the first 5 seconds
description: duration:5 keeps the opening of the 52 s Sintel trailer (no start: from 0), scaled to 640 px wide as WebM. The source timeline highlights 0–5 s and the Duration row reads ×0.10.

title: Trim: 6 seconds from the middle
description: start:20 with duration:6 cuts the dragon chase out of the middle: the cut is exact (decoded from the keyframe before 20 s, frames before it dropped), so the result's first frame matches the source at 20 s when you play both.

title: Trim: the last seconds (titles)
description: start:47 without an end keeps everything to the end of the trailer, the closing title card: about 5 s. Seek the comparison near the end and both players show the same frame.

title: 9:16 vertical with bars (whole frame kept)
description: crop:1280:544 first removes the trailer's own letterbox, then the 2.35:1 picture is fitted into a 540×960 vertical frame with extend: nothing of the picture is lost, the empty top and bottom are plain dark bars (bg 101010), no blur. Compare with the crop recipe next to it.

title: 9:16 vertical crop, anchored left
description: After crop:1280:544 drops the letterbox, resize:fill to 540×960 covers the vertical frame and cuts the sides; gravity we keeps the left part of the shot instead of the centre. Wipe the slider to see which slice of the wide frame survives.

title: 1:1 square for feeds
description: The letterbox cropped away (crop:1280:544), then fill 720×720 centred: a square of the widescreen trailer for feed posts; the Dimensions row goes from 1280×720 to 720×720.

title: 4:5 portrait post
description: fill 576×720 (4:5, the tallest feed format) of the letterbox-free picture (crop:1280:544) with gravity ea: the right side of the shot is kept.

title: Rotate a vertical phone clip to landscape
description: rotate:90 turns the 406×720 NASA vertical video clockwise into a 720×406 landscape frame (after any display matrix); the Dimensions row swaps.

title: Mirror a vertical clip (selfie flip)
description: flip:1:0 mirrors every frame left to right: on-screen text reads backwards in the result while the sound is untouched.

title: Vertical clip in a 16:9 frame (pillarbox)
description: The 9:16 clip fitted into 1280×720 with extend: black bars left and right, the whole picture kept, ready for a landscape player.

title: 60 → 30 fps
description: The 1080p60 Big Buck Bunny clip at fps:30, 960 px wide: every other frame dropped. Play at 0.5× in the comparison: the source stays smooth, the result steps; the Frame rate row reads 60 → 30.

title: 60 → 24 fps (film cadence)
description: fps:24 resamples the 60 fps clip to film rate: fast pans judder a little, the file shrinks; compare Bytes with the 30 fps recipe.

title: Quality ladder: CRF 20
description: The same 6 s cut at 854×480 in VP9 with crf:20 (close to the source and the largest file). Load the three CRF recipes in turn and compare the Bytes and Bit rate rows; zoom into the wipe to see the detail go.

title: Quality ladder: CRF 30
description: The same 6 s cut at 854×480 in VP9 with crf:30 (the usual web balance). Load the three CRF recipes in turn and compare the Bytes and Bit rate rows; zoom into the wipe to see the detail go.

title: Quality ladder: CRF 40
description: The same 6 s cut at 854×480 in VP9 with crf:40 (visibly soft in the dark and in motion; the smallest file). Load the three CRF recipes in turn and compare the Bytes and Bit rate rows; zoom into the wipe to see the detail go.

title: Codec: H.264 (gpl image)
description: video_codec:h264 in MP4 at quality:60, the same cut as the AV1 and VP9 recipes. quality maps onto each encoder's own CRF scale, so the three are the same setting, not the same picture: compare Bytes, then zoom into the wipe to judge detail per byte. libx264 is GPL: only the gpl image has it (disabled on full).

title: Codec: AV1
description: video_codec:av1 in MP4 at quality:60 (libaom, on the full and gpl images; the full image's default for MP4): compare the elapsed time, Bytes and detail with the H.264 and VP9 recipes of the same cut.

title: Codec: VP9
description: video_codec:vp9 in WebM at quality:60 (libvpx), the same cut as the H.264 and AV1 recipes: WebM plays in every current browser; compare Bytes and detail.

title: HEVC source → WebM for any browser
description: An HEVC (H.265) MP4, which many browsers cannot play (the Source side falls back to a still there), decoded and re-encoded as VP9 WebM at 960 px: the result plays everywhere.

title: Drop a silent audio track
description: The NASA rollout timelapse carries a stereo AAC track of pure silence; mute:1 drops it. The Audio codec row goes to none and Bytes shrink by the track's share.

title: Sound only: M4A (AAC) from a video
description: The m4a container drops the picture: 20 s of the trailer's soundtrack as AAC at 128 kbit/s. The result side is a waveform with an audio player; A/B (x) switches to the source's sound at the same moment.

title: Speech to MP3, mono 64 kbit/s
description: 30 s of the astronauts' message as a mono MP3 at 64 kbit/s (audio_channels:1): plenty for speech, a fraction of the video's bytes.

title: Speech to Opus at 24 kbit/s
description: The same speech as Ogg Opus at 24 kbit/s, resampled to Opus's 48 kHz: still intelligible at well under half the MP3 recipe's bytes; listen for the slightly papery top end.

title: Lossless FLAC of a piano recording
description: 20 s of the Chopin waltz as FLAC: lossless from the decoded MP3, so it sounds the same and takes more than twice the bytes of the same 20 s of MP3. FLAC ignores audio_bitrate.

title: Quiet speech → -16 LUFS
description: A LibriVox reading at about -23.6 LUFS normalised to -16 LUFS / -1.5 dBTP / LRA 11 (EBU R128 loudnorm, the podcast target): press A/B (x) while it plays and the source is clearly quieter.

title: Loud trailer → -23 LUFS (broadcast)
description: The trailer's soundtrack is mastered at about -13 LUFS with peaks over 0 dBTP; loudnorm to -23 LUFS / -1 dBTP (EBU R128 broadcast) brings it down about 10 dB without clipping: the opposite direction of the speech recipe.

title: Volume -12 dB
description: volume:-12dB lowers the piano by a quarter of its amplitude: the waveform shrinks to about a quarter of its height; A/B to hear the step.

title: Volume ×2 (+6 dB)
description: volume:2 doubles the quiet reading's amplitude; unlike loudnorm it is a fixed gain, so loud syllables can clip: compare the waveform peaks.

title: Fade in 3 s, fade out 4 s
description: fade:3:4 on a 20 s cut from the middle of the waltz: the waveform ramps up from silence and back down, where the source keeps playing at full level.

title: Stereo pan sweep → mono
description: A tone that pans left → right → left, downmixed with audio_channels:1: on headphones the source moves between your ears, the result stays in the middle; the Channels row goes 2 → 1.

title: Resample 48 kHz → 22.05 kHz
description: sample_rate:22050 halves the sample rate of the trailer's music: everything above 11 kHz (cymbals, air) is gone, which A/B makes obvious; the Sample rate row reads 48000 → 22050.

title: Waveform: stereo channels apart
description: split_channels draws one band per channel (1200×240 PNG, teal on white): the pan sweep shows as two bands that swell and shrink in turn.

title: Waveform: wide banner on dark (WebP)
description: A 1600×160 orange-on-charcoal WebP of the waltz's first minute (duration:60, the demo's output limit), mono (channels mixed): phrases and the louder passages are easy to see.

title: Waveform: transparent speech thumbnail
description: No background colour: a 600×120 transparent PNG of the reading's first minute, to lay over any player; the pauses between lines are the gaps.

title: Logo in a corner for the whole clip
description: The fixture logo (wmu) 16 px from the top-right corner at 85% opacity, scaled to 12% of the frame, on every frame (no window): the slider wipe shows it only on the result side.

title: Lower third that fades in and out
description: A Pango text overlay (wmt) bottom-left, shown from 1 s to 7 s of the output (overlay_window) with 0.5 s fades (overlay_fade): watch it appear after a second and leave before the end.
pipelines: Expedition 72 Thanksgiving from the ISS

title: Seconds counter on a timelapse
description: timecode:seconds in the bottom-right corner, 32 px amber at 90%: a running count of the output's seconds over the rocket rollout.

title: Chessboard watermark over a clip
description: The badge fixture (wmu) tiled as a chessboard (wm position ch) at 30% opacity on every frame: the proof-copy look, hard to crop out of a video.

title: 3 s silent loop (a GIF replacement)
description: 3 s of the 60 fps clip at 24 fps, 480 px wide, muted, as WebM: the kind of short loop sites used to ship as a GIF, at a fraction of the bytes; the result player loops it.

title: HLS: three renditions, 4 s segments
description: stream:hls:720:480:240 with segment_duration:4 over the first 24 s of the trailer: a master playlist with three renditions in CMAF segments, each transcoded when a player asks for it. Safari plays it; other browsers list its playlists.

title: DASH of a vertical clip
description: @mpd answers a DASH manifest; the rungs (720 and 360) are the short side, so a 9:16 source gets 720×1280 and 360×640 renditions in 2 s segments.

title: The untouched source (raw:1)
description: raw:1 streams the source bytes unmodified, with byte ranges, under the same signing and limits: what the comparison plays on its Source side. Every other option is ignored; Bytes match exactly (×1.00).

title: The untouched audio file (raw:1)
description: raw:1 on an MP3: the original file with its own Content-Type (audio/mpeg), nothing transcoded or cached.

title: /q/video: music to Opus
description: The query form on an audio source: duration, format=opus and audio_bitrate as query keys; 20 s of the waltz at 96 kbit/s.

title: Cloudinary: fetch, trim, resize, f_auto
description: Cloudinary's /video/fetch/ on a public URL: so_12 and du_6 cut, w_640 with c_limit scales down, f_auto answers WebM to clients that accept it and MP4 otherwise (Vary: Accept).

title: Cloudinary: ac_none drops the sound
description: ac_none removes the audio stream (the timelapse's silent track), f_webm writes WebM: the Cloudinary spelling of mute:1.

title: Cloudinary: e_volume:mute with q_auto
description: e_volume:mute (or e_volume:-100) silences the trailer while q_auto:eco picks a lower quality; other e_volume levels are not mapped yet (400 in strict mode).

title: Cloudinary: l_text layer in a time window
description: A text layer placed by its fl_layer_apply component bottom-left, shown from 1 s to 5 s of the output (so_, eo_ in the layer group) with a 0.6 s fade in (e_fade:600).

title: Cloudinary: sp_sd adaptive streaming (HLS)
description: sp_sd with f_m3u8 asks for an HLS master playlist with the standard-definition profile's 480, 360 and 240 renditions of a 20 s cut.

title: ImageKit: ik-master.m3u8 with sr-
description: ImageKit's adaptive streaming URL on a video file key: /ik-master.m3u8 with tr=sr-240_360 answers an HLS master playlist with 240p and 360p renditions.

title: ImageKit: l-text shown from 1 s to 4 s
description: An l-text layer on a video, 24 px from the bottom-left corner, with lso-1 and ldu-3 (start and duration on the output's timeline): the caption appears after a second and leaves at 4 s; f-webm writes WebM.

title: Cloudflare: mode=video with time and duration
description: Cloudflare Media Transformations on a public URL: time=12s and duration=5s cut, width=640 with fit=contain, audio kept (MP4: H.264 on the gpl image, AV1 on full).

title: Cloudflare: mode=audio from a 5.1 trailer
description: mode=audio extracts 15 s of the Big Buck Bunny trailer's six-channel AAC as stereo M4A (a source over two channels is downmixed).

title: Cloudflare: mode=frame as PNG
description: mode=frame takes one still at time=20s, 640 px wide, as PNG: a poster image from the same URL family (an image path; needs FFmpeg only).

title: Cloudflare: mode=spritesheet over 40 s
description: Twelve 160×90 frames spread over the first 40 s of the trailer (imageCount=12) in one JPEG grid: a scrubbing preview.

title: Smart crop
description: resize fill to a square with gravity sm: libvips' attention strategy keeps the interesting part.

title: Face crop
description: gravity obj:face centres the crop on the detected faces (YuNet).

title: Blur faces
description: blur_detections blurs every detected face with sigma 12: privacy in one option.

title: BlurHash and ThumbHash (/info)
description: Opens the Info tab with the placeholders the server computes (BlurHash 4×3, ThumbHash, dominant colours), decoded in the browser next to a thumbnail.

title: GIF → MP4
description: An animated GIF re-encoded as an MP4 video (H.264 in the gpl image, AV1 in full): a fraction of the bytes.

title: Video sprite sheet
description: video_thumbnail_tile: a 4×2 grid of 160×90 frames, one every half second.

title: PDF page 2
description: page:1 (0-based) renders the second page of a PDF, fitted to 600 px.

title: Camera RAW preview
description: A DNG demosaiced by LibRaw and delivered as a JPEG.

title: UltraHDR gain map → HDR AVIF
description: gain_map:hdr applies the UltraHDR gain map and keeps the HDR rendition in an AVIF (view on an HDR display; gain_map:sdr keeps the SDR base).
